todaysEvents.summary: Saudi oil exports recover via Hormuz
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 21 that Saudi exports recovered to just over 4 million bpd in September from 2.4 million bpd in August; Saudi oil through Hormuz averaged 2.9 million bpd over the past six days versus 700,000 in August.

todaysEvents.summary: Houthi attacks widen Saudi route risk
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 21 that Houthi attacks hit sensitive sites in Riyadh and an Aramco facility in Yanbu. AP reported Sep 20 that the Houthis warned against countries joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen.

Reuters reported Sep 21 that the US and Iran remain in a stalemate. No verified signed reopening is approved; QatarEnergy force majeure remains through November and the latest LNG transit observation remains carried.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: After the shelved talks resume, the Oman framework is signed and monitored; a restored, verified reopening lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks remain shelved or resume without regional consensus; traffic stays selective under Iranian fees and sanctions pressure; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while QatarEnergy seeks replacement LNG.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran enforces its threatened Hormuz exclusion zone, talks fail, or the tanker war widens into a broader multi-front exchange; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
